gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Styro crowds its letters shoulder to shoulder, with e and c nearly sealed shut. Noto Sans Old Sogdian is its opposite: tall lowercase, wide-mouthed forms that stay crisp, and a page of it feels clean and approachable.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Styro brings a retro, commanding look with tightly shut letters. Noto Sans Old Turkic sits beneath it with open curves and chunky, tall lowercase, so the pair's strongest quality is the tug between that closed-up heading and a body that stays wide open.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Commanding and retro, Styro packs its letters tight.  Noto Sans Oriya gives a longer read generous gaps in its curves and small letters nearly as tall as the capitals, so the lines feel approachable and contemporary.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-osage: Chunky, crowded, unmistakably retro up top. Noto Sans Osage fills its lines with inflated lowercase bowls and sweeping curves that never close, so Styro's tight letters get a roomy, approachable counterweight right below.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Styro presses its letters so close that the e and c nearly seal shut, a retro, commanding trait. Osmanya's sans handles the quiet work: wide s turns and oversized lowercase.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Retro and commanding, Styro crowds its letters until the e and c barely gap. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong loosens everything below it, with a high-set x-height and rounds left slightly cracked open like a bangle.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Commanding and retro, Styro squeezes its letters nearly shut at the e and c. Noto Sans Palmyrene lets curves stop short instead of closing in, with compact ascenders that keep the body modern and clean.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Styro's most striking trait is how tightly its letters crowd, leaving e and c barely open. And Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau feels like a window thrown open beside it, with open-ended curves and a short step from lowercase to capital.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Styro is the retro, commanding one, pressing its letters together until the e and c nearly close. But Noto Sans PhagsPa does the gentler work, with see-through c openings and a soft rise from small letters to capitals.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Styro leads with a retro, commanding swagger, its crowded letters almost sealing every e and c. Noto Sans Phoenician answers the heading's tightness with s curves open wide at both ends and generous lowercase height.
